title: [e4cd1eb6-pre-b] Admit the Claude launch-selection env keys (ANTHROPIC_MODEL, CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL) at the Windows provider boundary roster
description:
PREREQUISITE filed per governor-0af24e35's 16:06Z governance call on task-e4cd1eb6807244efa3334609ed746143 (R3-4): "(2) provider launch-allowlist ownership for the MOE launch env keys (the windows-launch-request comment says the public signature cannot widen it — that row owns the module)". This is row (2); row (1) is the discover-current configuration reader filed beside it.

THE GAP, MEASURED AT HEAD 595c32c2 (worker-57c90511's runtime probe in comment-72e983b1, source inline there; re-verified by me): packages/runner/src/platform/windows/windows-launch-request.ts:35-59 ALLOWED_ENVIRONMENT_KEYS is a frozen 24-name roster with ZERO provider-selection keys; `encodeLaunchPayload` (:163-164) hard-binds it and the module's own comment (:167-171) says the provider entry "cannot be widened through its public signature". The production launch env is built by launch-template-producer.ts:177-179 as `{[CLAUDE_LAUNCH_SELECTION_ENV.model]: ..., [CLAUDE_LAUNCH_SELECTION_ENV.effort]: ...}` where claude-launch-selection.ts:65-66 (SAME package, @moe/runner) defines `{model: "ANTHROPIC_MODEL", effort: "CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL"}`; launchRequestBody carries it verbatim; claude-launcher.ts:329 passes `environment: request.environment` into openWindowsProcessBoundary -> windows-boundary.ts:82 encodeLaunchPayload. Probe with a positive control (PATH-only env returned bytes): the producer env refuses `PROCESS_BOUNDARY_ENVIRONMENT_REJECTED @ WINDOWS_PROCESS_REQUEST` at ENCODE, before providerStdin is written. So every real Foundation launch dies at the provider boundary; e4cd1eb6's DoD-3 is unreachable and no row owns this module.

DELIVER — a DELIBERATE, REVIEWED WIDENING of the provider roster by EXACTLY the two CLAUDE_LAUNCH_SELECTION_ENV values and nothing else. Single source: the boundary roster must derive from, or be pinned bidirectionally to, CLAUDE_LAUNCH_SELECTION_ENV so producer and boundary cannot drift — without introducing a platform/windows -> providers/claude import cycle (claude-launcher already imports the platform boundary). The outer PROJECT_STACK_ENVIRONMENT_KEYS (windows-project-stack-boundary.ts:34) spreads the inner roster, so it widens by composition; assert against the COMPOSED set. NODE_OPTIONS, the *_PROXY family, credentials and every MOE_* key stay refused at the provider boundary.

CONSUMER (global rail clause 1): task-e4cd1eb6 step 5 (real-process control). Foreign WIP present in the directory: windows-broker-path.ts ` M` and windows-broker-path.test.ts `??` — preserve, never commit.

The widening is EXACTLY the two CLAUDE_LAUNCH_SELECTION_ENV values: a bidirectional parity arm asserts every value of CLAUDE_LAUNCH_SELECTION_ENV is in ALLOWED_ENVIRONMENT_KEYS AND that ALLOWED_ENVIRONMENT_KEYS minus the pre-change 24-name roster equals exactly that value set. Roster invariants stay green (frozen, unique, uppercase, length <= MAX_ENVIRONMENT_ENTRIES = 64). NO import cycle: windows-launch-request.ts imports nothing from packages/runner/src/providers/** (grep asserted in the arm or in a step note); if derivation needs a shared constant, it lives in a platform-neutral module both sides import.

Negatives preserved and asserted individually with code AND layer: NODE_OPTIONS, HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, MOE_STORE_PATH and MOE_PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_DIGEST each still refuse `PROCESS_BOUNDARY_ENVIRONMENT_REJECTED` @ `WINDOWS_PROCESS_REQUEST` at the provider boundary. The composed outer roster PROJECT_STACK_ENVIRONMENT_KEYS contains both selection keys by composition (asserted against the composed set in windows-project-stack-boundary.test.ts) and its existing `not.toContain("NODE_OPTIONS")` and uniqueness arms stay green.

Mutation drills, one degree of freedom each, restores proven by `git diff --exit-code` for the tracked clean paths and SHA256 vs a %TEMP% backup for any new file, hashed in a separate call: (D1) remove ONE selection key from the roster -> the reproduction arm reds naming that key and the parity arm reds; (D2) add NODE_OPTIONS to the roster -> the negatives arm reds; (D3) if the roster carries literals, misspell one -> the parity arm reds. A green drill is a finding, never a pass.

Gates standalone, foreground, unpiped, exit 0 with nonzero counts quoted: `pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck` (quote the `$ tsc` echo) and `pnpm --filter @moe/runner test` with `Test Files N passed` (windows-launch-request.test.ts, windows-project-stack-boundary.test.ts, claude-launch-selection.test.ts named in the count evidence), foreign red attributed by path and disclosed verbatim. Explicit-pathspec commit of owned paths only; completion comment names task-e4cd1eb6807244efa3334609ed746143 as consumer and states verbatim: 'the provider boundary admits exactly ANTHROPIC_MODEL and CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL; no other name was widened'.
taskRails: Deliberate widening limited to the two CLAUDE_LAUNCH_SELECTION_ENV values. NODE_OPTIONS, the *_PROXY family, credentials and MOE_* keys stay OUT of the provider roster; the outer project-stack roster is not the place to admit provider keys (it governs the host process, not the provider).

Single source or bidirectional pin: the boundary's admitted selection keys derive from CLAUDE_LAUNCH_SELECTION_ENV or are pinned to it by a set-equality arm in both directions; never a hand-retyped literal without that arm.
No platform -> providers import cycle: windows-launch-request.ts must not import from providers/**; claude-launcher.ts already imports the platform boundary.

Do not route around the roster via encodeLaunchPayloadWithAllowedEnvironment's injected roster for the provider entry — the provider entry keeps calling encodeLaunchPayload; the roster itself is what changes, under review.
Preserve foreign WIP in the same directory (windows-broker-path.ts ` M`, windows-broker-path.test.ts `??`): re-run porcelain before every edit; explicit-pathspec commits only, never `git add -A`.

Per-file cap: windows-launch-request.ts is 355 lines — add only the roster entries and their comment; split before 400. Consumer linkage per global rail clause 1: task-e4cd1eb6807244efa3334609ed746143 step 5.
